doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The houses and neighborhood in Pontiac
summary: He names the three houses he lived in and describes the business-district neighborhood near the church.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you remember the street address of the house you grew up in, in Pontiac

Oh yes! It was 129 Bagley Street. No I’m sorry! The first house, the house I was born in was Orchard Lake. That was the name of the street, Orchard Lake. We moved from there when I was about ten, we moved up into a bigger house up the street from there, about 6 blocks or so. And that was 74 Orchard Lake.
We moved from there to another part of town. It was 129 Bagley Street.
And that’s the house you remembered?
Can you describe what the neighborhood was like, who was living there?
Oh yes. It was like sort of in the business part of town. My uncle had a drycleaners there and people had stores and it was very industrious. The church was very near there.
